sections.title: Players, Victory and Scoring
sections.text: Two players begin at 24 composure and zero accord. Reduce the opponent to zero composure, or reach eight accord by completing Undertakings. State checks occur after the entire effect sequence or simultaneous combat batch. If both qualify at that check, the result is a draw. After turn 120 ends, compare composure + 3 × accord; a tie is a draw. Arcade rewards are 60 coins for a win, once per match; losses and draws award nothing. No real money or purchased cards.

sections.title: Decks, Zones and Opening
sections.text: A deck is exactly 30 catalog cards, at most two of a card ID. All eight types and all six circles may mix without colour restrictions. Each player draws six; once before the first turn, the human may shuffle the entire hand back and draw six (free mulligan). The first player does not draw on turn one. Zones are deck, hand, two battlefield districts, discard and exile. Every current card is a catalog card; this edition has no token-creation effects. No sideboard, hidden counters or collection purchases.

sections.title: Turn Structure and Timing
sections.text: A seeded coin chooses the first player. The active player refreshes their Neighbors, once-per-turn activations, and focus; start-of-turn effects resolve in battlefield insertion order, then draw one (except the first player first turn). Main actions may be taken in any order: play cards, activate abilities, or make individual attacks. Each attack opens a defender window. The defender may play Sparks and then block or allow the hit. Resolution returns to the same main phase, so main actions can follow combat. End turn discards chosen cards until at most nine remain, then starts the other turn. There is no stack or counterspell system: each action resolves atomically, in the order of its structured effects. Sparks may be played in your own main phase or your defender window, never during an effect resolution.

sections.title: Focus and Homesteads
sections.text: On each of your turns, your base focus capacity increases by one to a maximum of ten. Refresh focus to base capacity plus your Homestead count (maximum three). Unspent focus is not carried into a refresh. All costs are generic. Play at most one Homestead per turn; it costs zero and immediately adds one focus. Homesteads cannot be attacked or targeted. Expanded Homesteads may have settlement effects when played and start-of-turn effects, which resolve after battlefield start effects in settlement order. Their art represents a resource district, not a separate draw requirement. A full Homestead zone makes further Homestead cards unplayable.

sections.title: Card Types and Space
sections.text: Database Creature = Neighbor, Instant = Spark, Sorcery = Ritual, Artifact = Tool, Enchantment = Habit, Land = Homestead, Planeswalker = Envoy, Battle = Undertaking. These are catalog taxonomy labels, not imported commercial rules. Each district (Porch and Square) holds up to three Neighbors per player. Each player has four support slots shared by Tools, Habits, Envoys and Undertakings; choose a district for each. Sparks and Rituals resolve and go to discard. All other non-Homestead cards remain until scattered or exiled. Passive attack and armor bonuses affect only friendly Neighbors in the support district and disappear as soon as that support leaves.

sections.title: Attacks, Blocks and Simultaneous Damage
sections.text: A Neighbor may attack once on its controller turn if ready and not newly arrived; Quick bypasses arrival delay. Choose an enemy player, enemy Envoy or enemy Undertaking in its district, or work on your own Undertaking in that district. Enemy Neighbors are not directly attacked: they may block. Each enemy-directed attack opens a defender window, even against an Envoy or Undertaking. Any ready Neighbor in that district may block; if a ready Guard exists, one of those Guards must block. Blocking exhausts the blocker and prevents damage to the declared target, except Pierce overflow to the defending player. Attacker and blocker deal combat damage simultaneously; subtract armor separately from each damage packet, minimum zero. Unblocked attacks damage their declared target. Working on your own Undertaking cannot be blocked and causes no retaliation. Attacking normally exhausts the attacker; Steady does not, but never permits a second attack that turn. Health damage persists; there is no end-turn regeneration.

sections.title: Effects, Targets and State Checks
sections.text: Card effect IDs refer to effects.json operations; printed descriptions are generated from these records and never parsed as code. Chosen targets must satisfy their target rule both when paid for and resolved; an illegal action changes nothing. Growth increases current and maximum health together. Armor is persistent for a permanent; aura armor is recalculated. Recall removes bonuses and arrival status by returning the base card to hand. Exile bypasses scattering and death triggers. Zero-health Neighbors and Envoys, and defeated Undertakings, leave simultaneously before their death/completion effects resolve in battlefield insertion order. Siphon heals only actual combat damage, capped at target remaining health; Pierce overflow is a separate packet. Empty-deck draws cause accumulating fatigue damage: one on the first failed draw, two on the second, and so on. Full lane/support spaces reject a play before costs are spent.

sections.title: Undertakings and Envoys
sections.text: An Undertaking has a printed work value (health). Your Neighbors in its district may spend their attack to reduce that value. When your work finishes it, discard it, gain two accord and draw one card. Opponent attacks may destroy it without giving either player accord. An Envoy has health but no combat attack; it is a support with a once-per-turn activation costing one focus. Certain Tools also have activations. An activation can only occur in the owner main phase. New supports can activate immediately. A support without a printed activation has none.

sections.title: Dice, Randomness and Determinism
sections.text: Pocket Weather rolls a d6: 1-2 heal three, 3-4 draw one, 5-6 deal three to the opponent. Dice do not change attack accuracy: attacks do not roll to hit. Deck shuffles, the starting player coin and dice use the match seed. Given the same seed, decks and legal action sequence, the engine produces the same state. The computer uses its own hand and public information only, not the human hand or either deck order. It obeys the same legal action generator.

sections.title: Catalog and Openness
sections.text: The library contains 226,400 uniquely named card records, four times the original catalog, across all eight types. The original 56,600 records retain their IDs and contents. Forty-eight curated cards anchor 52 starter decks with 50 new explained variations; expansions combine structured operation recipes and statistics. They are not all independently designed, illustrated or balance-tested. Forty-eight local AI-generated illustrations are reused by type and faction with per-card tinting. Catalog, effects, keywords, rules, starter decks, schema, generator and engine source are available as local files. See LICENSE.txt, ART.md and CONTRIBUTING.md for the scope of the licenses. No official commercial game cards, text, logos or artwork are imported.
